meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to know who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Before we go further, on what basis was it entered?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
A seventeen-year-old put on the spot in a hallway can blank on a word, Hale. You said you wrote it down the same day, so show me that note with its date on it.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale. That's called revising. Put the outline and the essay in front of me, with the dates, and I'll read them myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's 4.4, and nothing on his record is the part I need. But I haven't seen the note or the outline, and I won't take a rewrite for something I can't check. Show me those, and the writing comes tonight, not Friday.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record, but I accepted nothing. I still require the note from November 2 and the October 15 outline shown to me with their dates, the zero withdrawn, and the offer put in writing tonight. You said you would send it by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with the zero still to be withdrawn, although your offer met her demand about his record; she still wants the documents and the offer in writing tonight, and her time had not run out. A private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4 is the fair outcome, and you named it, but she would not take it without seeing anything.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one sentence and moved on, which earned a flat Okay and the first small sign of ground.
What cost ground: You described a hallway question and an outline but never put either document in front of her, so your evidence stayed a claim she could not check, and offering the rewrite before showing it let her refuse it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence touched October only through the date of the outline, not that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see the note, slide it across with its date before you mention the outline, and hold the rewrite offer until she has read both.
